newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended the day lower, undermined by worries before Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee FOMC) meeting in the U.S.
The market was also skittsh before a tender for new federal Swiss bond issues Tuesday, expected at about 0600 GMT.
Traders generally expected a two-tranche offering, with the longer tranche likely to be a reopening of an existing bond.

Many traders believe the current 4-1/2 percent April 2006 benchmark has become too expensive for the market, and they expected the Swiss Treasury to instead reopen an outstanding 4-1/2 percent June 2007, or a 4-1/4 percent January 2008 issue.

One trader said the current small amount of liquidity in the 4-1/2 percent 2007 would argue for a reopening of that issue. But the 4-1/4 percent 2008 would be preferable for the market in terms of yield, as it is cheap relative to other paper.

Traders also expected a shorter tranche, which would provide deliverable paper for the Swiss futures exchange's new Comi medium-term bond contract. That issue could possibly reopen the outsanding 4-1/2 percent June 2000 issue, traders said.
